title: Pause and Options redesign: grouped Pause, Options rail, gear on the menu bar
summary: The Pause menu is one panel with its rows grouped by purpose. Options has a side rail with live preview on wide screens and a plain list of categories on a portrait phone. The main menu status bar has a gear that opens Options from any page with the bar.
details: Pause: the ride's own actions come first, then Options and Jukebox, then sharing, then leaving. A landscape phone shows the groups in two columns so nothing scrolls.
Rows show what they do: a switch for On/Off, the value between arrows for a choice, and a chevron for a row that opens a page. Back and the list pagers sit in a footer that does not scroll.

Options on wide screens (640 px or more between the side safe areas) keeps the categories in a rail beside the open category's rows. Q/E and the pad's shoulder buttons change category. Escape steps back to the rail.
Options on a portrait phone is a list of categories, each with a line saying what it holds.
Options opened over a menu page uses the same panel. The status bar gear opens it from any page that shows the bar.
Labels, values and saved keys still come from the shared menu definitions, so the rules did not change.
Also in this change: a launch flag opens Pause or Options for a native capture, and the menu diagnostics report the layout.
limitation: Checked in desktop captures and browser tests at 1280×720, 844×390 and 390×844. Not checked on a physical phone or with a real controller. The shoulder-button category switch has no automated test. Three older browser tests (menu parity, ride songs, soundtrack) fail the same way on production and are tracked separately.
caption: Pause on desktop: the rows are grouped, and the list ends in Copy ride link.
verification: Host only: 191 atv-ui tests pass, including controller tests for the wide and narrow paths. tools/test_engine_options_layout.mjs passes on desktop, landscape phone, portrait phone and the gear. Of 30 existing browser tests that drive these menus, 27 pass; the 3 failures match production. After merging main, the menu, pause, photo, replay and layout tests pass. Native captures of every page were inspected.
